answer: Fingerprint-Split Secret Sharing. Each identity’s signing key is split: one shard embedded in a pearl-like token, one wrapped in a cipher tied to the agent’s runtime fingerprint, one derived from an umber-coded time offset. Duplicating an agent clones all shards, so both copies produce identical signatures on the same challenge. The rule: any two signatures from one fingerprint on distinct nonces trigger a reveal, forcing the attacker to rebuild the entire shard set per clone—paying full key-generation and re-enrollment cost each time.
